what_it_does: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is a technique for automatically discovering the best neural network layout for a given task or device, instead of a human engineer designing it by hand. A "supernet" is a single massive network that contains many possible sub-architectures inside it; once trained, you can slice out a smaller network tailored to any target device without retraining from scratch. The problem is that training a supernet from zero takes 72 to 83 GPU-days, which is very expensive. SuperFast dramatically cuts that cost by first training a small, fast sub-network within the supernet and then spreading what that small network has learned across the full supernet before the expensive main training begins. This warm-start means the supernet needs far fewer training steps to reach good accuracy, acting as a plug-in speedup compatible with existing supernet frameworks.
